---
title: Getting started
description: Install HTSeqCountCluster and prepare an explicit sample manifest.
---

Counting many BAM files one at a time requires repeated manual submissions.
HTSeqCountCluster instead submits one `htseq-count` task per BAM file to Slurm
or PBS/Torque. Version 2.0 requires Python 3.10 or newer and HTSeq 2.1 or newer.

## Background

HTSeqCountCluster began with a problem I ran into while working with many BAM
files. I wanted a simple way to use more than one core without managing every
count job by hand, so I opened an [issue on the HTSeq
repository](https://github.com/simon-anders/htseq/issues/43) to ask about it.

That conversation sparked this project. The idea is straightforward: give each
sample its own `htseq-count` job, then bring the results together in one count
table.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install HTSeqCountCluster
```

The installation provides the command-line interface. Each batch task must run
in an environment that also provides:

- `htseq-count`
- HTSeqCountCluster

How you configure that environment remains site-specific.

## Prepare a sample manifest

Create a two-column CSV file:

```csv
sample_id,bam_path
control-1,/data/rnaseq/control-1.bam
treated-1,alignments/treated-1.bam
```

The two columns have separate roles:

- `sample_id` is the sample identifier.
- `bam_path` locates the alignment file.

Relative BAM paths resolve from the manifest directory. Sample identifiers must
be unique and cannot contain directory separators.

Each task writes `<sample_id>.counts.tsv` to the output directory.

## Preview before submitting

Before using cluster resources, run the same request as a dry run. A dry run:

- validates the manifest, BAM files, and annotation;
- writes the scheduler scripts; and
- does not call `sbatch` or `qsub`.

```bash
htseq-count-cluster run \
  --scheduler slurm \
  --dry-run \
  --infile samples.csv \
  --gtf genes.gtf \
  --outpath counts
```

Review the generated command and scripts before submitting.

The files remain under `counts/.htseq-count-cluster/<submission-name>/`. They
preserve the inputs needed to understand or diagnose the job later.
